postconditions.satisfied_by: tc4 RULED: the seam earns a durable anchor, but NOT a docs/architecture node. Anchored as a named section in docs/CONSTELLATION_OVERVIEW.md ('The install and instantiation chain: one source, three live copies') carrying the layer chain, the constraint, three measured instances (#501, #439/#446/#484, the Admiral's own pre-fix spine.json waiver), and the verification pointer to ComposedShippedArtifactTests. Earns an anchor on Inclusion Rule 'rule preservation' + 'trust'. Refused a docs/architecture node for three independent reasons: (1) no graph exists to add to -- a one-node map is ceremony; (2) #456 is in flight and owns where map surface lives, so hand-building a competing tree pre-empts it; (3) the seam is invisible to a derived AST map anyway -- hop one is a file copy, hop two is text substitution, neither is a reference edge -- so #456 landing does not retire this anchor. Not promoted to capability: it is a constraint on structure, not something the system does. Intended future node shape recorded in the reconcile artifact so the id need not be re-derived. Index/overlay ceremony: N/A, none exists.

triage_candidates.statement: No check compares an installed or instantiated copy against its source. install_constellation.py writes hop one (bundle) and init_work_area.py writes hop two (spine.json); nothing verifies either afterwards. Measured three times in epic 418: #501, #439/#446/#484, and the Admiral's own spine.json instantiated pre-fix and waived. Current truth is recorded in docs/CONSTELLATION_OVERVIEW.md 'The install and instantiation chain'; remediation is future work. The fix is NOT obvious -- what a running agent holding a stale copy should do (re-instantiate, refuse, warn) is a real design question, and this epic's own no-mid-wave-re-install ruling is evidence the answer is not 'always refresh'.

ROUTE TO #528 AS EVIDENCE, NOT A NEW ISSUE. #528 asks whether markdown templates belong in the derived map and as what. Architecture answer from this reconcile: the architecturally significant property of a shipped template is not its extension and not its content schema -- it is that it is copied and then instantiated, so each has up to three live copies at different ages. That property is invisible to a *.json glob (528's own finding) AND invisible to an AST-derived map (neither hop is a reference edge). So extending the sweeps from .json to .md widens the wrong axis, and #456's map will not close it either. The verification #528 reaches for is a copy-vs-source comparison -- the sibling candidate tc1 -- which applies identically to both extensions. Draft comment text is in .agent-work/epic-418-redux/ARCHITECTURE_RECONCILE.md; NOT posted, this run leaves edits in the tree.

why_trail.why: This repo ships the Cartographer but has never run one on itself: docs/architecture/ has no history at all. So the reconcile has no map to diff against, and the architecture record of record is docs/CONSTELLATION_OVERVIEW.md plus docs/agents/*, which is what epic-298's reconcile also used. That reframes tc4 from 'add a node' to 'there is no graph to add it to', and makes the ruling turn on where durable structural truth actually lives here.

The net change is 9 source/doc files; only two of them moved a claim the durable record makes. The engine and crew-context changes had already been reconciled by the waves that made them, which is why the reconcile finds little -- worth saying, because a near-empty reconcile reads like a skipped one otherwise.

The float asked for a map id and the honest answer is that there is no map. Ruling on where the record belongs mattered more than ruling on the seam, because putting it in a new docs/architecture tree would have collided with #456 while adding no coverage the derived map can ever give.

Compliance here is a statement about an absent map, and an absence reported as a pass is the failure mode this corpus keeps finding in its own checks -- so it is recorded as an open structural question instead. The candidates carry the real remediation.
